what: A handover inspection is the documented walk-through done when a property is delivered by the developer to the buyer. It identifies every defect, every snag, every incomplete finish that should be on the record before you take occupancy.

Defects liability period. This is a contractual warranty written into the sale and purchase agreement, most commonly twelve months from handover, covering non-structural items: MEP, HVAC, leaks, doors, windows, fittings, finishes, cracks and alignment. No UAE law fixes it at twelve months and no law obliges a developer to grant one. Check your own SPA.

Decennial liability. This is a statutory ten-year protection that cannot be waived. It covers total or partial collapse and defects threatening the building's stability or safety. Under the UAE Civil Code the contractor and supervising engineer are jointly liable for ten years from delivery. Article 40 of Dubai Law No. 6 of 2019 holds the developer liable for ten years from the completion certificate for structural defects in jointly owned property. For facts and acts on or after 1 June 2026 the federal provisions are renumbered under Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025, with the former Articles 880 to 883 applying before that date.
A cracked tile is the defects liability period. A cracked structural column is decennial liability.

If you need a professional handover or snagging inspection. Specialist firms send a technician to test systems and appliances on site. That is a different service from a documentation app.

steps.body: The defects liability period, if you have one, lives in the sale and purchase agreement. Note the start date, the duration, and how defects must be notified. Nothing on this page replaces that document.

steps.body: Timing is the whole point. Defects noted after you have signed acceptance are easier for a developer to treat as yours. Walk the unit while it is still empty, with the lights on and water and power live if you can.

steps.title: Look at finishes, then systems
steps.body: Walls, floors, ceilings, doors, windows, grout, paint, and alignment first. Then taps, drainage, AC, sockets, appliances, and any smart-home kit. Photograph every issue in context and close-up.

steps.title: Put it in writing and send it
steps.body: A list with photos, unit number, handover date, and a request for a written acknowledgement. Email it to the developer's customer-care channel named in your SPA, and keep the thread.

steps.title: If the developer refuses to engage
steps.body: You still have the dated record. Chase in writing, escalate through the channel in the SPA, then to the competent authority for the type of defect. A photographic file is not a substitute for a specialist snagging report, but it is better than a memory.

steps.title: Then document the rental, if you let the unit
steps.body: Once a tenant moves in, the relevant document is a check-in signed by landlord and tenant, not a developer snag list. That is the flow Snagify is built for.

faqs.answer: A thorough first walk of a new 1BR apartment often takes 60 to 90 minutes; a villa longer. Better to take the time than to discover defects after the contractual window, if you have one, has started running.

A useful snag list names the unit, the date, and each defect with its location, a short description, and photographs. Send it in writing to the developer or contractor named in your contract, keep the delivery record, and chase a written acknowledgement.

If they ignore it, escalate through the channel in your sale and purchase agreement. For contractual finish defects that sits with the defects liability period, if your SPA grants one. For structural safety, that is a different legal track: decennial liability.

You walk the same rooms, photograph the same angles, and AI highlights changes between then and now. Pre-existing damage is excluded automatically. Only new damage is up for discussion. The PDF includes both inspections.

steps.title: Schedule the move-out
steps.body: 1-2 days before key handover. Both parties present. Allow 30 to 45 minutes for the walk-through.

steps.title: Pre-clean professionally
steps.body: Done before the inspection, not during. A spotless property settles disputes before they start.

steps.title: Pull the check-in baseline
steps.body: Snagify auto-loads the original check-in. Pre-existing damage is visible in the comparison view.

steps.title: Walk the same flow
steps.body: Same rooms, same order. Photograph each room's current state. AI compares to check-in and flags changes.

steps.title: Discuss each flagged item
steps.body: For each new item AI flags, agree with the landlord whether it's wear and tear, your responsibility, or theirs. Each decision is documented.

faqs.question: When should I schedule my move-out inspection?
faqs.answer: Ideally 1-2 days before you hand back the keys. This gives you time to fix small issues before they become deductions. Avoid scheduling on the same day as your move-out, you'll be too rushed.

faqs.question: Should I clean before or during the inspection?
faqs.answer: Before, ideally professionally. A spotless property settles disputes before they start. Show up to the inspection with the property in the same clean condition you received it.

faqs.question: What counts as 'fair wear and tear' in Dubai?
faqs.answer: RERA's general guidance: minor wear from normal use is the landlord's responsibility (paint fade, light scuffs, carpet wear). Damage from negligence or accidents is the tenant's (broken fixtures, stains, holes in walls). The dividing line is reasonableness. The Snagify report records both views; the RDC weighs them.

faqs.question: What if the landlord insists on charging for pre-existing damage?
faqs.answer: Show them the original check-in photos that documented the damage. If they still insist, they can take the case to the RDC. With a Snagify check-in and check-out both signed, your case is overwhelmingly strong.

faqs.question: Can I do a move-out without the landlord present?
faqs.answer: Technically yes, but it's not recommended. A move-out without the landlord's signature is weaker evidence. If they refuse to attend or sign, document the refusal in the report. The unsigned report is still legal evidence.

what: A rental deposit in Dubai is typically 5% of the annual rent for unfurnished and 10% for furnished. That is market convention, not a legal figure: Dubai tenancy law requires the deposit to be returned at the end of the tenancy but does not fix its amount. The landlord holds it for the duration of the tenancy and is supposed to return it at move-out, minus deductions for damage beyond fair wear and tear.

In practice, most landlords keep some portion of the deposit for vague reasons: 'cleaning fee', 'paint touch-up', 'deep cleaning', 'damage that wasn't documented at check-in'. Without strong tenant evidence, these claims often stand.

Deposit protection isn't a legal mechanism in Dubai (unlike the UK's tenant deposit scheme). It's a documentation discipline. Tenants and landlords who document their inspections thoroughly get their deposits handled fairly. Those who don't, fight for them. For the full recovery playbook, read how to get your security deposit back in Dubai.

faqs.question: How big is a typical Dubai deposit?
faqs.answer: Market practice is 5% of the annual rent for an unfurnished property and 10% for a furnished one. On a AED 100,000 tenancy that is AED 5,000 or 10,000. These are conventions, not legal figures: Dubai tenancy law requires the deposit to be returned at the end of the tenancy but does not fix its amount.

faqs.question: Is the deposit held in escrow in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Unlike the UK's tenancy deposit scheme, Dubai doesn't have a third-party deposit holder. The landlord holds your deposit directly. This is one reason documentation matters so much: there's no neutral party verifying the funds.

faqs.question: What's the most common reason tenants lose deposits?
faqs.answer: Lack of documented check-in. The landlord claims damage existed when the tenant moved out that wasn't there at move-in. Without a Snagify-style baseline, the tenant has no evidence to dispute the claim. The deposit stays with the landlord.

faqs.question: How long does the landlord have to return my deposit?
faqs.answer: Dubai tenancy law expects deposits to be returned within a 'reasonable timeframe' after move-out, typically 1-3 weeks. There's no strict legal limit. If your landlord delays unreasonably, you can file at the RDC.

faqs.question: What if my landlord refuses to use Snagify?

dilapidations-dubai.subheadline: A formal record of a property's condition at the start and end of a lease, used to determine which party is responsible for damage and disrepair beyond fair wear and tear. Snagify produces evidence-grade dilapidations reports.
what: Dilapidations is the legal term for damage and disrepair in a leased property attributable to the tenant. A schedule of dilapidations is the formal report identifying every item the tenant must restore at the end of the lease.

In Dubai, dilapidations are most commonly used in commercial leases (office, retail, warehouse) where the financial stakes are higher and the lease terms are more detailed. They're also used in high-value residential tenancies (luxury villas, branded residences) where landlords want strong contractual recourse.

A Snagify dilapidations report contains dated photographs, a written record of condition, signatures from both parties when they sign, and a verification hash. UAE law recognises electronic documents and signatures; admissibility and weight are for the court or committee to assess case by case.

scenarios.body: A formal dilapidations report at the start of the lease protects your asset and sets clear expectations. At the end, it's the document the courts use to assess your reinstatement claim.

faqs.question: Is dilapidations the same as a check-out inspection?
faqs.answer: Related but more formal. A check-out inspection is the everyday inspection at end of tenancy. A dilapidations report is the formal legal document used in commercial leases and high-value residential tenancies, usually with explicit reference in the lease contract. Snagify can produce both.

faqs.question: Do I need a dilapidations report for a residential tenancy?
faqs.answer: Usually no. A standard check-in and check-out is sufficient for most residential tenancies. Dilapidations is most relevant for commercial leases (where the figures are larger and the contracts more detailed) or for luxury residential tenancies where the landlord wants formal contractual recourse.

faqs.question: When in the lease should the baseline be recorded?
faqs.answer: At handover, before the tenant takes possession. If you're already mid-tenancy without a baseline, an interim dilapidations report is still better than none, though its evidentiary weight is reduced compared to a true pre-tenancy baseline.

faqs.question: How long does a commercial dilapidations inspection take?
faqs.answer: Commercial dilapidations are more thorough than residential check-outs. Plan for 90 to 180 minutes for a small office or retail unit, 3 to 5 hours for a larger commercial space.

faqs.question: Can a Snagify dilapidations report be used in court?
faqs.answer: UAE law recognises electronic documents and signatures. Admissibility and weight are for the court or committee to assess case by case. The report contains dated photographs, both parties' signatures when they sign, and a verification hash.
